title: Native RNA G quadruplex immunoprecipitation (rG4IP) from mammalian cells
protocol: Centrifuge cells at 200 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Resuspend and wash the pellet with ice-cold PBS followed by centrifugation, repeat PBS wash.
Resuspend the pellet in 400 μL of ice-cold rG4IP lysis buffer.
Incubate cells with lysis buffer in an end over end rotator at 4°C for 10 min.
After incubation, centrifuge the cells at 2,000 × g for 5 min at 4°C to pellet the nuclei.
Pipette out and save the supernatant: this is the cytosolic fraction (lysate).
Save 10% of the lysate as an Input control for normalization.
Thoroughly resuspend Protein G magnetic beads in their solution and transfer 100 μL to a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube.
Magnetize the beads and remove the supernatant.
Wash the beads thrice with PBS-T, thoroughly resuspending each time before discarding the supernatant after magnetization.
Add the lysate to the washed beads and incubate for 1 hour at 4°C in an end over end rotator.
Briefly centrifuge and magnetize the beads after incubation, then pipette out the lysate for further use with the bound antibody.
Thoroughly resuspend Protein G magnetic beads in their solution and transfer 100 μL to a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube for antibody binding.
Magnetize the beads and remove the supernatant.
Wash the beads thrice with PBS-T, thoroughly resuspending each time before discarding the supernatant after magnetization.
Incubate the beads with 3 μg of BG4 antibody or equivalent isotype-matched negative antibody control.
Incubate in an end over end rotator for 1 hour at 4°C.
Briefly centrifuge the beads after incubation.
Resuspend the beads in PBS and magnetize to discard supernatant.
Repeat washing three times.
Add pre-cleared lysate to the antibody-coated beads.
Incubate between 6 to 10 hours at 4°C in a rotator.
Magnetize the beads after overnight incubation.
Save the flow-through lysate.
Resuspend the beads in lysis buffer and incubate for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Repeat washing three times.
Place magnetic rack on ice during washing.
Optionally, increase washes to five times to reduce background signals.
Resuspend beads in 100 μL of nuclease-free water.
Incubate at 65°C for 15 minutes to release nucleic acids.
Magnetize the beads and transfer supernatant containing eluted nucleic acids into a new Eppendorf tube.
Add 10 μL of 10× DNase I Buffer to the eluted sample.
Add 1 μL of DNase I (2 U/μL) to the eluted sample.
Incubate for 15 min at 37°C.
Add 1 mL TRIzol reagent to the DNase treated sample.
Add 500 μL TRIzol to the input controls saved after digitonin treatment.
Invert the tubes 5 times.
Incubate at room temperature for 5 min.
Add 200 μL of chloroform per 1 mL of TRIzol used.
Shake the tube vigorously for 15 s.
Leave at room temperature for 5 min.
Centrifuge the tube at 12,000 × g for 15 min at 4°C.
Carefully remove the top aqueous phase without disturbing the interphase.
Transfer to a fresh tube.
Add 20 μg glycogen and vortex briefly.
Add 500 μL of 100% room temperature isopropanol per 1 mL TRIzol reagent used.
Invert the tubes 5 times.
Incubate at room temperature for 10–15 min.
Centrifuge at 12,000 × g for 30 min at 4°C to precipitate the RNA.
Remove the supernatant carefully.
Wash the pellet in 1 mL 75% ice-cold ethanol per 1 mL TRIzol reagent used.
Briefly vortex to get the pellet off the side of the tube.
Centrifuge at no more than 7,500 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Repeat the washing step with 75% ice-cold ethanol followed by centrifugation.
Carefully remove the ethanol using a pipette.
Then centrifuge again to collect the remaining ethanol.
Carefully remove the remaining ethanol.
Air dry the pellet for 2–3 minutes at room temperature.
Resuspend the pellet in 15 μL of nuclease-free water.
Use this whole volume to perform reverse transcription with random primers.
Use 1 μL of cDNA to perform quantitative real-time PCR.
